title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions and rollout hysteresis
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: The current performance canary detector occasionally causes rollout flapping and false positives for transient latency spikes and short throughput dips. This PR implements an enhanced auto-detection algorithm with hysteresis and improved baseline estimation to reduce noise-triggered rollbacks and give operators clearer signals. Changes include: 1) Exponential smoothing baseline for p50/p95/p99 latency with configurable alpha per metric; 2) Two-stage detection: short-window anomaly detector for immediate alerts plus sustained-window detector for rollout decisions; 3) Hysteresis/cool-down windows on canary rollouts to prevent flip-flop between variants (configurable cool_down_seconds and max_toggle_count); 4) Throughput drop detector that compares offered load vs observed throughput and triggers degraded rollouts if sustained; 5) Guard actions integrated with rollout service: pause, scale-down canary weight, and automated rollback after sustained deviation; 6) Canary simulator harness and deterministic unit/integration tests for detector behaviors; 7) Metrics and alerts: new canary.detector.* metrics, trace spans for detector evals, and dashboard panels for sustained deviation windows; 8) Backwards-compatible config schema with v1->v2 migration path. Testing and rollout: added unit tests, integration tests that exercise simulated canary traffic profiles, and perf-canary can be toggled in staging for 24h validation before production rollout. Related: ENG-2314 for detection algorithm, ENG-2890 for rollout guard requirements, SUP-412 customer incident that motivated hysteresis. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] load tests in perf lab, [x] console dashboard updated, [x] migration utility included. Rollout plan: staged deployment behind feature flag, 24h staging observation, gradual ramp to 10%/50%/100% with automatic rollback on sustained regressions.
